cells.tense: You are taking in what shows up here, and you can feel it move you.
cells.ask: Take the next thing that comes in today and give it ten minutes and your attention before you decide anything about it.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you're taking it in without a fight. No forcing, no waiting for a better moment — it comes in, it lands, and it moves you toward the next thing. You probably don't notice that happening.

This is how it looks running right: you sit with what showed up long enough for it to change something small. A turn in your day, a different route, a call you make because of what you heard. Nothing dramatic, nothing forced. You already do this. Stay where you are and let one more thing come in the way the last one did, and let it decide what you do next.
cells.sheetLine: You're meeting what arrives, and it shapes your next move.
cells.verb: letting what arrives land in one direction
cells.place: the threshold where what is outside comes in, and you get to decide how to meet it

cells.tense: You are already living in what is about to arrive, bracing at a door that hasn't opened.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're getting ready for and write down what's already in your hands for it — the real pieces, not the plan.
cells.core:
You're bracing for what's coming instead of taking in what's here. The next thing lands almost any minute, and you're already inside it, guessing how it will go, moving things around to be ready. Bracing feels like getting ready. It keeps you from letting anything actually land.

Gone right, you're not standing in next week. You meet today's arrival with attention, and what you do next grows out of it. Some of what you're preparing for already came in and you walked past it. Take one thing that's here now and give it your full attention for as long as it takes. Direction starts from what landed, not from what might.
cells.sheetLine: You're meeting what hasn't arrived and missing what has.
cells.verb: letting what arrives land in one direction
cells.place: the threshold where what is outside comes in, and you get to decide how to meet it

cells.tense: You are standing where you were when the last thing came through, not letting anything else in.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing that reached you this week, without deciding yet what it means.
cells.core:
Something came through and didn't make it all the way in. You watched it arrive and then held it there, and you're still where you were when it stopped. Nothing new gets in because the last thing that arrived is still in your hands, unopened.

Meeting what comes is something you can do. In working order it's ordinary: something reaches you, you take it in, and you let it sit long enough that it starts to matter. Pick one thing from this week, small and plain, whatever reached you, and let one person hear it. You don't have to know what it means yet. Getting it out of your hands is where the movement starts.
cells.sheetLine: You can meet what arrives. You stopped after one didn't.
cells.verb: letting what arrives land in one direction
cells.place: the threshold where what is outside comes in, and you get to decide how to meet it

cells.tense: You are already taking things in and calling it that you don't care what comes.
cells.ask: Name one thing you took in this week and what you did with it, out loud, as yours. Once is enough.
cells.core:
You're letting things in and it's shaping what you do next. That part is running. What's missing is you saying so. When someone asks what you're working toward, you shrug, or you say it doesn't matter yet, or you say nothing's arrived — and meanwhile you've been walking around with what came in, changing your route because of it.

Nobody handed you that direction. You took it in. Say that once — pick one thing that reached you and say you chose it. Not a plan, not a promise. Just the plain fact that something came in and you were the one who let it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been taking it in. You still call it nothing.
cells.verb: letting what arrives land in one direction
